title: The birth of Linux
description: On 25 August 1991, Linus Torvalds announced a 'free operating system (just a hobby, won't be big and professional like gnu)'. Today Linux runs the majority of servers, all top supercomputers, and Android.

title: Kubernetes came from Borg
description: Kubernetes was created at Google, inspired by their internal cluster manager Borg, and donated to the CNCF in 2015 as its first project.

title: The GPL flips copyright into copyleft
description: The GNU General Public License uses copyright law to guarantee freedoms to use, study, share and modify software — a legal hack invented by Richard Stallman.

title: openSUSE and SUSE Linux
description: SUSE, founded in Germany in 1992, is the oldest existing commercial Linux distribution and stewards the openSUSE community project.

title: Digital sovereignty in the EU
description: The EU defines digital sovereignty as Europe's ability to act independently in the digital world, leveraging open source as a strategic lever.

title: Drupal powers governments
description: Drupal is used by whitehouse.gov, the European Commission, and many other public institutions thanks to its strong content modelling and open governance.

title: The Unix philosophy
description: Write programs that do one thing well, and work together. Doug McIlroy's 1978 maxim still shapes microservices and cloud-native design today.

title: Tim Berners-Lee gave away the Web
description: In 1993 CERN released the World Wide Web software into the public domain, ensuring an open, royalty-free Web for everyone.

title: Ada Lovelace, first programmer
description: In 1843 Ada Lovelace published the first algorithm intended for a machine — Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine.

title: RFCs built the Internet
description: Request for Comments documents, started by Steve Crocker in 1969, are the open, consensus-driven backbone of Internet standards.

title: Supply chain security with Sigstore
description: Sigstore provides free signing, verification and provenance checks for open source artifacts, hosted under the OpenSSF.

title: Containers without Docker
description: Kubernetes moved away from the Docker shim in 1.24, embracing the container runtime interface with runtimes like containerd and CRI-O.

title: GAIA-X and European cloud
description: GAIA-X aims to build a federated, sovereign data infrastructure for Europe, based on open standards and interoperability.

title: Linus's Law
description: 'Given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow.' Eric S. Raymond's principle from The Cathedral and the Bazaar captures the power of open collaboration.

title: The principle of least privilege
description: First articulated by Saltzer and Schroeder in 1975, every program and user should operate with the minimum privileges necessary to complete the job.
